shortDescription: Britain on Tuesday appointed William Sargent to lead a revived cross-government body charged with identifying outdated rules and reducing regulatory burdens on businesses and public services.($1 = 0.7667 pounds)

children: Britain on Tuesday appointed William Sargent to lead a revived cross-government body charged with identifying outdated rules and reducing regulatory burdens on businesses and public services.
Better Regulation Executive was restored in the budget to drive regulatory reform
Finance ministry said the executive would help deliver the government's target of cutting regulatory administrative burdens by 25% by the end of parliament
Government says target is equivalent to savings of £5.6 billion ($7.30 billion) and 280 million working hours a year
It says it has made £2 billion of net progress towards that goal
Previous Better Regulation Executive had reported more than £3.5 billion of annual savings for businesses and voluntary organisations between 2005 and 2010
Sargent, who also chaired the body then, will work with ministers and regulators to identify outdated and duplicative rules
